scope.author_separation: Reviewer authored replication_requests.py schema extension separately. This is not an independent review of that owned record-store implementation. Reviewed CLI/Policy/coordinator/loop production changes and the cwd correction were authored by root/runtime; no edits to those sources by this reviewer.
scope.execution_boundary: Actual completed CPU source is produced through existing CLI/Orze/native supervised path. The boundary under test is real data-only CLI admission from another caller cwd, followed by exact-key replay; no second worker is launched by replicate.

findings.symptom: Exact absolute -c from another cwd returned exit 2/error 'execution: loaded CPU configuration changed', after source was already TERMINAL and its reservation SETTLED.
findings.cause: CLI loaded and stamped the CPU configuration within config_path.parent, restored caller cwd, then invoked cpu_execution through the public service. Cwd is intentionally part of the frozen CPU fingerprint.
findings.correction: Root kept runtime validation, existing-Lake opening and request service invocation inside the exact project cwd try, restoring caller cwd in finally. Fingerprint was neither erased, weakened nor recomputed to grant a different context.

findings.result: BoundPolicy validates exact Replicate fields and the detached original completed full Ref, not a callback-mutated view. Coordinator passes and repeats expected_source_ref inside its owned transaction. Replicate creates a queued mapping then durable Wait, not a worker/claim/reservation; ordinary Execute performs CPU replication authorization before reserve/claim.

Request verification checks current source/target/request rows, exact metadata digests, effect receipts and route witnesses. It does not hash all artifact content or rerun a domain interpreter. B source capture and native GO/publication gates remain separate. Same config/spec and distinct observations do not establish scientific correctness, hermetic execution or statistical independence.
